claim: After starting a transform (G/R/S) and constraining it to an axis, typing an exact numeric value (e.g. R then 90, or S Y then 3) and pressing Enter applies that transform precisely, rather than relying on approximate mouse-drag placement -- useful whenever a build calls for an exact rotation or scale factor rather than an eyeballed one.
supporting_evidence: Direct quote (11:18-11:23): "when you press R, you can actually type in the degrees that you want it to rotate... If I press 90 now, that will go exactly 90 degrees and I can press enter"; and (12:10-12:20): "Scale Y. And I could actually type in three here and it will scale three times. And then I'll press enter."
rejected_alternative: Eyeballing the rotation/scale by dragging the mouse until it looks roughly right
